institutionName: Institut d'études politiques de Paris (Sciences Po)

questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I had been on a visit to Paris when my friends were on ERASMUS there and I really enjoyed the city. This motivated me to get my own experience of living there. I also really wanted to practice my spoken French and thus the language was a significant aspect in determining my destination.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: My overall experience was very good, although it sometimes did take some energy to understand a whole new system and educational approach.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: I thought it was fairly easy to find the sufficient information. The process of applying for courses was confusing however.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: We received e-mails with information. I chose not to partake in the introductory days, however, so thus was probably informative as well although I cannot speak to it.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: I am quite satisfied. It was nice, however, to share the experience with a few fellow students from Copenhagen, so we could share information amongst ourselves.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: Quite easy! I lived in the Cité Universitaire and can highly recommend it.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Cité Universitaire is a bit far south, but has a lively community feeling.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I can highly recommend the Cité Universitaire and was very satisfied with the student community there.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The registration process was chaotic and confusing.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: As stated above, the registration process was chaotic and confusing. One had to log on at a very specific point in time and it was difficult to figure out whether or not I had succeeded in registering for the courses which I wanted.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: We had received some e-mails prior and there was also an informative video. However, the process was still confusing and stressful.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Very unsuccessful. I succeeded only in getting one course which I wanted.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Have some friends by your side to help you create an overview of the courses which you get and don't get on the day. Don't have high expectations with regards to wanting specific courses.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I definitely found it interesting to experience a different academic programme than the one I came from. However, the courses varied quite a bit with regards to level and expectations.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I generally found the level of courses to be lower than the one I am used to at Copenhagen University. The courses all seemed less 'academic' and more 'practical' than I am used to. However, I cannot know if this is specific to the courses I ended up taking.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: It was different with regards to student participation. People participated quite a bit more in discussions than at UCPH, which was nice. We also had to prepare more student presentations than at UCPH which was a good learning experience.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Gender Economics

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Costs with regards to housing, e.g. buying a duvet and pillow.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Being 26+ years old, museums were more expensive than anticipated.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I have not participated in any non-academic opportunities at the host institution, but instead spent more energy at the housing place (Cité Universitaire). However, it is my impression that there were many opportunities.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Unsure. More information would probably have been good, since I did actually want to partake in sports but was unsure how to.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I did not participate in any at the host institution. I can, however, highly recommend participating in things at Cité Universitaire (e.g. sports pass).

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Take the train around France and visit some other areas. I personally visited Lyon, Tours, Nice, Antibes, Ville Franche sur Mer, Marseille, Rouen and Annecy.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: It was quite easy since I already knew the culture from growing up in an international environment in Brussels.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Live in the Cité Universitaire and do sports there!!

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Not much.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The livelihood and going out atmosphere. The international and open community spirit in the Cité Universitaire was also great.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Do not expect to be able to take the courses that you want.
Prepare yourself well for the course registration process (prepare a list of 20+ courses).
Consider living in the Cité Universitaire and getting to know students from all over the world.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: I cannot think of anything besides the three things listed above.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Being part of an openminded international community (again). Enjoying the spirit in Paris of being independent and spending time by oneself in a city full of opportunities.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Adjusting to the different educational system and approach (e.g. not knowing the requirements for each course since they vary quite a bit).

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: Enjoy Paris if you do go!

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
